hints.title: Check the logarithm’s order
hints.body: Use its definition to compare log1/2(1/2) and log1/2(1), and decide whether input order is preserved.
hints.recap: The base determines the direction of logarithmic order.
hints.pitfall: Applying the same function to both sides does not always preserve an inequality.
hints.pause: Use that order behaviour when auditing the logarithm step.

recall.reminder: The base determines the direction of logarithmic order.

hints.title: Check each later operation separately
hints.body: Evaluate the divisor log1/2(1/4) and determine its sign; also check the hypotheses of the logarithm power rule.
hints.recap: Each step is judged relative to the preceding line.
hints.pitfall: A false inherited inequality does not make every subsequent transformation invalid.
hints.pause: Check the division, arithmetic and integer interpretation on their own merits.

recall.reminder: Each step is judged relative to the preceding line.

hints.title: Compare with a common-base solution
hints.body: Rewrite the original powers using base 1/2, then compare their exponents using the order of that exponential.
hints.recap: A second method can check an inequality’s direction.
hints.pitfall: Keep the strict endpoint when converting to an integer condition.
hints.pause: Solve independently, then identify which displayed transition has the inconsistent direction.

recall.reminder: A second method can check an inequality’s direction.

solution:
Step I is invalid: log1/2 is decreasing, so the inequality must reverse. The later power law, division by the positive number 2, arithmetic and integer interpretation are valid transformations of their preceding lines.

Correctly, (1/2)2n<(1/2)50 gives n>25, hence n≥26. Only I is invalid: answer B.
knowledgePattern: Locate order reversal under a logarithm with base below one
